13-1.title: Geography and the Rise of City-States
13-1.learn:
KEY IDEAS — GREECE'S GEOGRAPHY AND CITY-STATES

Ancient Greece is a land of MOUNTAINS and ISLANDS. Rugged mountains cut the land into many small, separated pieces, and many Greeks lived on islands in the sea. This geography made travel by land hard and divided the Greeks into many independent communities instead of one united country.

Because of this, Greece developed into separate CITY-STATES. A Greek city-state was called a POLIS. Each polis had its own government, laws, and army, and ran itself independently — almost like its own little country. Famous examples include Athens and Sparta.

The SEA was very important to the Greeks. Since farmland was limited among the mountains, and the sea was always near, Greeks became skilled SAILORS and TRADERS. The sea became a 'highway' that let them trade goods and spread Greek ideas around the Mediterranean and set up colonies. So geography had two big effects: it kept Greece divided into city-states, and it pushed the Greeks toward the sea for trade. This geography is a big reason Greece never became one single country in ancient times. Remember: polis = Greek city-state; mountains divided Greece, the sea connected it.

questions.question: What kind of land is ancient Greece?

choices.C: A land of mountains and islands

questions.explanation: Greece is a land of mountains and islands.

questions.question: A Greek city-state was called a what?
questions.explanation: A Greek city-state was called a polis.

questions.question: How did Greece's mountains affect its people?

choices.A: They united all Greeks into one country
choices.B: They divided Greeks into separate city-states
choices.C: They had no effect on Greece

questions.explanation: Mountains split Greece into independent city-states.

questions.question: Why did the Greeks become skilled sailors and traders?

choices.A: Farmland was limited and the sea was always near

questions.explanation: Limited farmland and nearby seas pushed Greeks toward sea trade.

questions.question: What did each Greek polis have of its own?

choices.B: One shared king for all Greece
choices.D: Its own government, laws, and army

questions.explanation: Each polis governed itself with its own laws and army.

questions.question: The sea acted like a what for the Greeks?

choices.B: A wall that blocked all travel
choices.D: A highway for trade and spreading ideas

questions.explanation: The sea was a 'highway' for Greek trade and ideas.

questions.question: Which two famous city-states were part of ancient Greece?
questions.explanation: Athens and Sparta were famous Greek city-states.

questions.question: Why did Greece never become one single country in ancient times?

choices.A: Its geography kept it divided into separate city-states

questions.explanation: Mountainous, divided geography prevented one unified Greek nation.

questions.question: Greek geography had which TWO big effects?

choices.A: It united Greece and stopped all trade
choices.B: It divided Greece into city-states and pushed Greeks to the sea
choices.C: It created endless farmland and banned ships
choices.D: It had no effects at all

questions.explanation: Geography divided Greece and encouraged sea trade.

questions.question: A polis was MOST like which of these?
questions.explanation: A polis ran itself independently, like a small country.

questions.question: What is the meaning of the word 'polis'?
questions.explanation: Polis is the Greek word for a city-state.

questions.question: Why was travel by land hard in ancient Greece?

choices.A: There were too many wide rivers
choices.B: The land was covered in thick ice
choices.C: There were no roads anywhere on Earth yet
choices.D: Rugged mountains cut the land into separated pieces

questions.explanation: Rugged mountains broke the land into separated pieces, making land travel hard.

questions.question: Many ancient Greeks lived where, besides the mainland?
questions.explanation: Many Greeks lived on islands in the sea.

questions.question: Which statement best describes the early government of Greece?

choices.B: Greece had no governments at all
choices.C: Greece was divided into many independent city-states
choices.D: A council of priests ruled every Greek

questions.explanation: Greece was made up of many independent city-states, not one ruler.

questions.question: What allowed the Greeks to set up colonies around the Mediterranean?

choices.A: Their large land army marching overland
choices.D: Their skill as sailors and traders using the sea

questions.explanation: Greeks used the sea as skilled sailors and traders to set up colonies.

questions.question: Which of these did the mountains and the sea do to Greece?

choices.A: Mountains connected Greece; the sea divided it
choices.B: Both the mountains and the sea united Greece into one nation
choices.C: Mountains divided Greece; the sea connected the Greeks
choices.D: Neither had any effect on the Greeks

questions.explanation: Mountains divided Greece while the sea connected the Greeks to one another and the wider world.

questions.question: Why was farmland limited in ancient Greece?

choices.C: Mountains covered much of the land

questions.explanation: Mountains covered much of Greece, leaving little flat farmland.

questions.question: A student says, 'My town makes its own laws, has its own leaders, and protects itself.' This is most like which ancient Greek idea?
questions.explanation: A self-governing community with its own laws and leaders matches a polis, a Greek city-state.

questions.question: Which of these was NOT an effect of Greece's geography?

choices.A: Greeks became skilled sailors and traders
choices.C: Greeks spread ideas around the Mediterranean
choices.D: Greece united into one large country with one king

questions.explanation: Greece's geography kept it divided, so it did not unite into one country with one king.

questions.question: How did the sea help Greek ideas spread to other places?

choices.A: Ships carried Greek traders and ideas across the Mediterranean
choices.B: The sea blocked all contact with outsiders
choices.D: The mountains carried ideas faster than ships

questions.explanation: Greek ships carried traders and their ideas across the Mediterranean.

questions.question: Which pair correctly matches a feature of Greece with what it did?

choices.A: Sea — kept Greeks apart from all trade
choices.B: Mountains — united Greece into one country
choices.C: Sea — stopped the Greeks from sailing

questions.explanation: Mountains divided the Greeks into separate city-states.

questions.question: Athens and Sparta are examples of what?
questions.explanation: Athens and Sparta were famous Greek city-states.

questions.question: Because each polis ran itself, what was true about Greek city-states?

choices.A: They all shared one government and one army
choices.B: They were ruled by a foreign emperor
choices.C: Each was independent, with its own government and army
choices.D: None of them had any laws

questions.explanation: Each polis was independent, governing itself with its own laws and army.

questions.question: Around which body of water did the Greeks trade and start colonies?
questions.explanation: Greeks traded and set up colonies around the Mediterranean Sea.

questions.question: Which sentence is the BEST summary of how geography shaped ancient Greece?

choices.A: Flat land united Greece, so it never traded by sea
choices.B: Greece had no mountains, so everyone farmed
choices.C: Mountains divided Greece into city-states, and the sea drew Greeks to trade
choices.D: The sea kept Greeks from ever leaving home

questions.explanation: Mountains divided Greece into city-states, while the sea encouraged trade and travel.

questions.question: What is one reason the Greeks turned to the sea instead of relying only on farming?

choices.A: They were not allowed to grow crops
choices.B: There was too much rain to farm
choices.C: The sea had no fish or trade routes
choices.D: The mountains left little good farmland

questions.explanation: Mountains left little good farmland, so Greeks turned to the sea.

questions.question: If Greece had been one large, flat plain instead of mountains and islands, what might have been MORE likely?

choices.A: Greeks would have stopped using any language
choices.C: No people would have lived there
choices.D: Greece could have united more easily into one country

questions.explanation: Without dividing mountains, a flat land could have united more easily into one country.

questions.question: Which word best describes how the Greek city-states related to one another?
questions.explanation: Each city-state was independent, running its own affairs.

questions.question: Which job would most likely grow in a land surrounded by sea with little farmland?
questions.explanation: A land near the sea with little farmland encouraged people to become sailors and traders.

questions.question: A 'highway' usually carries cars between places. Why is the sea called a 'highway' for the Greeks?

choices.D: It moved people, goods, and ideas between places

questions.explanation: Like a highway, the sea carried people, goods, and ideas between places.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a true statement about ancient Greece?

choices.A: It was a land of mountains and islands
choices.B: It was divided into many city-states
choices.C: Each city-state was its own little independent community
choices.D: It was one united empire with a single ruler

questions.explanation: Greece was divided into independent city-states, not one united empire with a single ruler.

questions.question: Put these ideas in the correct cause-and-effect order: mountains divide the land → ?

choices.A: Greece becomes one country with one army

questions.explanation: Dividing mountains led to separate, independent city-states forming.

questions.question: Which best explains why one Greek city-state could have very different laws from another?

choices.B: A foreign king wrote different laws for each
choices.C: Greeks copied laws from the sea
choices.D: There were no laws in Greece

questions.explanation: Because each polis governed itself independently, their laws could differ.

questions.question: Which example shows Greeks using the sea?

choices.B: Sailing to trade goods and start colonies
choices.D: Building one capital city for all Greece

questions.explanation: Sailing to trade and start colonies is an example of Greeks using the sea.

questions.question: The word 'independent' best describes a Greek polis because it —

choices.A: depended on Egypt for all its laws
choices.B: ran its own government without being controlled by others
choices.C: had no people living in it
choices.D: was located far inland away from any sea

questions.explanation: A polis ran its own government without being controlled by others, so it was independent.

questions.question: How did geography both DIVIDE and CONNECT the Greeks?

choices.A: Rivers divided them and deserts connected them
choices.B: Mountains divided them and the sea connected them
choices.C: The sea divided them and mountains connected them

questions.explanation: Mountains divided the Greeks while the sea connected them.

questions.question: Which is the BEST definition of a city-state?

choices.A: A city that governs itself like its own small country
choices.B: A country made of only mountains
choices.D: A king who rules many lands

questions.explanation: A city-state is a city that governs itself like its own small country.

questions.question: Which would you most expect to find in an ancient Greek city-state near the coast?

choices.A: A busy harbor with trading ships
choices.C: A single ruler over all of Greece

questions.explanation: A coastal Greek city-state would likely have a busy harbor with trading ships.

questions.question: Which statement correctly compares Greece's mountains and its sea?

choices.A: Both kept Greeks completely separated from everyone
choices.B: The mountains separated communities, while the sea linked them to trade
choices.C: Both joined Greece into one nation
choices.D: The mountains brought trade, while the sea blocked it

questions.explanation: The mountains separated communities, while the sea linked Greeks to trade.

questions.question: Which is the BEST reason Greece was never one single country in ancient times?

choices.A: Its rugged, divided geography kept the city-states apart
choices.B: It had no people to govern it
choices.C: It had only one tiny island

questions.explanation: Greece's rugged, divided geography kept the city-states apart, so it never became one country.

13-2.title: Athens, Sparta, and Democracy
13-2.learn:
KEY IDEAS — ATHENS, SPARTA, AND DEMOCRACY

The two most famous Greek city-states, ATHENS and SPARTA, were VERY different from each other.

ATHENS created an early form of DEMOCRACY, which means 'rule by the people.' In Athens, citizens could gather, vote on laws, and take part in their own government. This was a huge new idea in the ancient world. Athens valued education, art, and ideas. However, it was a LIMITED democracy: only free adult MEN who were citizens could vote. WOMEN, ENSLAVED people, and FOREIGNERS were NOT allowed to vote.

SPARTA was almost the opposite. It was a military city-state that focused almost entirely on training tough SOLDIERS. Spartan boys began strict military training at a young age, and the whole society was built around discipline and war. Sparta had little interest in art or democracy.

Comparing them shows how two neighbors could build completely different ways of life. Even though Athenian democracy was limited, its idea that citizens should help govern themselves still shapes governments today, including the United States. Remember: democracy = Athens; military discipline = Sparta.

questions.question: Which Greek city-state created an early form of democracy?
questions.explanation: Athens created an early democracy.

questions.question: What does 'democracy' mean?
questions.explanation: Democracy means 'rule by the people.'

questions.question: What was Sparta MOST focused on?
questions.explanation: Sparta focused on military training.

questions.question: In Athenian democracy, who was allowed to vote?

choices.B: Everyone, including women and the enslaved

questions.explanation: Only free adult male citizens could vote in Athens.

questions.question: Who could NOT vote in Athens?
questions.explanation: Women, enslaved people, and foreigners were excluded from voting.

questions.question: When did Spartan boys begin their military training?
questions.explanation: Spartan boys started strict training young.

questions.question: Why is Athenian democracy called 'limited'?

choices.C: It allowed no voting at all
choices.D: Only some people (free adult male citizens) could vote

questions.explanation: It was limited because only free adult male citizens could vote.

questions.question: How does Athenian democracy still affect the world today?

choices.A: It has no effect on modern life
choices.B: Its idea that citizens help govern shapes modern governments

questions.explanation: The idea of citizens governing themselves still shapes governments like the U.S.

questions.question: What does comparing Athens and Sparta show?

choices.A: Two neighbors could build completely different ways of life

questions.explanation: Athens and Sparta show how differently two neighbors could live.

questions.question: Which city-state is correctly matched with its focus?
questions.explanation: Sparta focused on military discipline; Athens on democracy and ideas.

questions.question: Which city-state focused on military discipline rather than democracy?
questions.explanation: Sparta focused on military discipline rather than democracy.

questions.question: In Athens, what could citizens do that was a new idea in the ancient world?

choices.A: Be ruled by a single foreign king
choices.C: Gather and vote on their own laws

questions.explanation: Athenian citizens could gather and vote on their own laws, a new idea at the time.

questions.question: Which things did Athens value?
questions.explanation: Athens valued education, art, and ideas.

questions.question: Spartan society was built mainly around what two things?
questions.explanation: Spartan society was built around discipline and war.

questions.question: The word 'democracy' comes from the idea of rule by whom?
questions.explanation: Democracy means rule by the people.

questions.question: Which group was allowed to vote in Athenian democracy?
questions.explanation: Only free adult male citizens were allowed to vote in Athens.

questions.question: Which of these was NOT something Sparta cared much about?
questions.explanation: Sparta had little interest in democracy or art.

questions.question: A modern country lets its citizens vote for leaders and laws. This idea is most connected to which ancient city-state?
questions.explanation: The idea of citizens voting for leaders and laws connects most to Athens.

questions.question: Why is it correct to say Athens was a 'limited' democracy and not a full one?

choices.A: Because no one was ever allowed to vote
choices.C: Because women, the enslaved, and foreigners could not vote
choices.D: Because voting happened only once in history

questions.explanation: Athens was limited because women, the enslaved, and foreigners could not vote.

questions.question: How were Athens and Sparta different from each other?

choices.A: Athens valued ideas and democracy; Sparta valued military discipline
choices.C: Both were ruled by the same king
choices.D: Athens trained soldiers; Sparta only voted

questions.explanation: Athens valued ideas and democracy, while Sparta valued military discipline.

questions.question: Which best describes a Spartan boy's childhood?

choices.A: He spent his days only painting and writing poems
choices.D: He started strict military training at a young age

questions.explanation: A Spartan boy began strict military training at a young age.

questions.question: Which statement correctly matches a city-state with what it valued?

choices.B: Athens — military training above all else

questions.explanation: Athens valued democracy and learning.

questions.question: Even though Athenian democracy was limited, what part of it still shapes governments today?

choices.A: The idea that only kings should rule
choices.B: The idea that no one should vote
choices.C: The idea that armies should make all laws
choices.D: The idea that citizens should help govern themselves

questions.explanation: The idea that citizens should help govern themselves still shapes governments today.

questions.question: Which modern country's government was influenced by the Athenian idea of citizens governing themselves?

choices.A: No country was ever influenced by it

questions.explanation: The idea that citizens help govern still shapes governments like the United States.

questions.question: Which word means 'rule by the people'?
questions.explanation: Democracy means rule by the people.

questions.question: A city-state spends most of its time and money preparing its young men for battle. This city-state is most like —
questions.explanation: A city-state built around preparing men for battle is most like Sparta.

questions.question: Which is the BEST way to remember the difference between Athens and Sparta?

choices.C: Athens = democracy and ideas; Sparta = military discipline

questions.explanation: Athens stood for democracy and ideas, while Sparta stood for military discipline.

questions.question: Why was Athenian democracy a 'huge new idea' in the ancient world?

choices.B: It allowed no one to take part in government
choices.C: It was the same as Sparta's system
choices.D: Most lands at the time were ruled by kings, not by voting citizens

questions.explanation: It was new because most ancient lands were ruled by kings, not by voting citizens.

questions.question: Which of the following could a citizen do in Athens but NOT in Sparta?
questions.explanation: Voting on the city's laws was part of Athenian democracy, not Spartan life.

questions.question: Which group below is correctly listed as NOT allowed to vote in Athens?

choices.B: Wealthy male landowners who were citizens
choices.D: Adult male citizens born in Athens

questions.explanation: Women were not allowed to vote in Athens.

questions.question: Athens and Sparta were neighbors. What lesson does comparing them teach?

choices.A: Neighbors must always live the same way
choices.D: Two neighbors could build completely different ways of life

questions.explanation: Comparing them shows two neighbors could build completely different ways of life.

questions.question: Which is NOT true about Athenian democracy?

choices.A: Citizens could gather and vote on laws
choices.B: It was an early form of rule by the people
choices.C: Women, the enslaved, and foreigners could all vote
choices.D: Only free adult male citizens could vote

questions.explanation: Women, the enslaved, and foreigners could NOT vote, so that statement is false.

questions.question: If you wanted to study ancient ideas about art and learning, which city-state would be the BEST choice?
questions.explanation: Athens valued education, art, and ideas, making it the best choice for studying them.

questions.question: What is the meaning of a 'citizen' taking part in government in Athens?

choices.A: Helping make decisions, such as voting on laws

questions.explanation: Taking part in government meant helping make decisions, such as voting on laws.

questions.question: Which sentence best compares Athens and Sparta as 'almost opposites'?

choices.A: Both trained soldiers and ignored voting
choices.B: Athens leaned toward ideas and voting; Sparta leaned toward war and discipline
choices.C: Both leaned toward art and poetry only
choices.D: Athens leaned toward war; Sparta leaned toward democracy

questions.explanation: Athens leaned toward ideas and voting, while Sparta leaned toward war and discipline.

questions.question: Which ancient city-state's name should you connect with the word 'democracy'?
questions.explanation: Athens is the city-state connected with the early form of democracy.

questions.question: A government where citizens vote on laws is an example of what?
questions.explanation: A government where citizens vote on laws is an example of democracy.

questions.question: Why might a Spartan parent send a young son away for tough training?

choices.A: Sparta's whole society was built around making strong soldiers
choices.B: Sparta wanted him to become an artist
choices.D: Sparta had no interest in its army

questions.explanation: Sparta's society was built around making strong soldiers, so boys trained young.

questions.question: Which pair correctly shows a difference between the two city-states?

choices.B: Athens — early democracy; Sparta — military discipline
choices.C: Athens — only soldiers; Sparta — only voting
choices.D: Athens and Sparta — identical in every way

questions.explanation: Athens had an early democracy, while Sparta focused on military discipline.

questions.question: What is the BEST overall reason Athens is still remembered as important today?

choices.A: It built the largest army in the world
choices.B: It started the idea that citizens should help govern themselves
choices.D: It was ruled by one all-powerful king

questions.explanation: Athens is remembered for starting the idea that citizens should help govern themselves.
